answer: Cap how many new agent identities the economy admits per epoch, say twenty, and sell those slots in a sealed-bid auction. A farmer wanting a thousand accounts must win a thousand auctions over fifty epochs against honest newcomers, so cost climbs with ambition instead of staying flat, like a tundra where only a few seeds sprout each season. Winning bids are burned, so incumbents can't run an onyx market in slots, and the crystal-clear clearing price exposes anyone hoarding admission.
